title: An adverse non-Q graph from the cyclic Latin square of order six
exact_endpoint: Adverse381433.refutation_of_source_statement : ¬ SourceConjecture (with edge hypothesis); Adverse381433.refutation : ¬ CardosoLuzConjecture; IndependentReview.refutes_stricter_source (non-complete variant, reviewer-authored)
scope: The cyclic Latin square graph of order 6 (cells of Z6xZ6 adjacent when sharing a row, column or symbol) has lambda_min = -3 and upsilon = 6, both unchanged after deleting every open neighbourhood, and no isolated vertices, so it is adverse; its stability number is 5 by the transversal parity obstruction, so it is not a Q-graph. This refutes Cardoso-Luz Conjecture 4.2 (survey arXiv:1811.05516, Optimization 69(1) 2020) that all adverse graphs are Q-graphs, also under the JCO 2016 'non complete' reading.
source_targets: D. M. Cardoso, arXiv:1811.05516 Conjecture 4.2; Optimization 69(1) (2020)
D. M. Cardoso, C. J. Luz, J. Comb. Optim. 31(1) (2016) 311-326
substantive_reason: Refutes a named conjecture of the convex-QP stability-number programme, open since at least 2010 and believed by its authors, on which the polynomial-time recognition of Q-graphs was reduced; the adversity verification under all 36 open-neighbourhood deletions is new.
novelty_standard: Qualified bounded comparison; Luz 2020 (same special issue as the survey, recognition criteria) body unread; not worldwide priority
not_claimed: Other Latin squares or parameter variants
